title: Strict Guard-Checking Machine
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite-state Turing machine $C$ over the Boolean alphabet, with at least four work tapes, an entry state, an injective map from $\\{0,1\\}$ to its states, and a constant $a\\in\\mathbb N$, such that the following holds. Whenever bit strings $x,bits,rest$ satisfy that the aligned pair parser applied to $x$ returns $(bits,rest)$, there is a time $t\\le a(|x|+1)$ at which, starting on input $x$ in the entry state with all work tapes blank, the machine is in the exit state indexed by whether $B_F(\\operatorname{val}(bits)+1)\\le |rest|$, where $B_F=\\max(\\operatorname{guard}(F),(4k+5)3^{k+1})$ and $\\operatorname{val}(bits)$ is the least-significant-bit-first binary value of $bits$. At that time its output is empty, its input-head position is $2|bits|+3$ if the inequality holds and $|x|+1$ otherwise, and every work tape except tape $1$ contains its prescribed ready word with its head at cell zero; moreover, no earlier time $u<t$ is in either exit state.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ has at least four work tapes
initial input is $x$, entry state, and all tapes blank
final state is the exit state selected by the guard inequality
no earlier visit to either exit state
all work tapes except tape 1 have the prescribed contents and head at zero
